data.narrative:
Space Machines Company is a Series A aerospace venture founded by Rajat Kulshrestha and George Freney, having raised AU$11M to date. The valuation universe comprises 5 public Space & Aerospace peers (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private comparables including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, and Planet Labs.

Of three valuation methods tested, only stage-progression proved applicable. This method uses the AU$11M total raised as a proxy for post-money valuation and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement to derive an implied valuation of AU$22M. Peer-median analysis was not feasible due to insufficient narrow-set peers meeting same-stage or adjacent-stage filters within Space & Aerospace—only 2 adjacent-stage comparables were identified, falling short of the three-datapoint threshold. Public-comp anchoring could not be applied because the target's revenue is not disclosed, precluding meaningful P/S multiple application against the sector median of 26.4x across public tickers.

The triangulated range is AU$19M (low) to AU$25M (high), centered on AU$22M. This narrow band reflects reliance on a single method and the limited direct comparability within the early-stage frontier aerospace market. Key uncertainties include the target's actual revenue trajectory, cash runway, and technical differentiation relative to the sparse peer set. Revenue disclosure or additional operating metrics would sharpen the valuation significantly.
